Centering of spending variables
```{r}
var_cent <- c("spnd_clothes", "spnd_debt", "spnd_edu", "spnd_entertain", "spnd_food", "spnd_goods", "spnd_household", "spnd_housing", "spnd_indv_donation", "spnd_med", "spnd_org_donation", "spnd_personal", "spnd_transport", "spnd_utility", "exp_material_exp", "exp_material_mat", "spnd_business", "time_save", "payment_amount_usd_stnd")

df_spend_cent <- gmc(df_spending, c(var_cent), "pid")
```


#Happiness with purchases by spending type

```{r}
#ICC
mlm1 <- lmer(payment_happy_comp ~ 1 + (1 | pid), data = df_spend_cent)
tab_model(mlm1)
```

Figure 1, Table S6
```{r}
#All estimates in a single multilevel model
mlm1 <- lmer(payment_happy_comp ~ spnd_utility_dev+ spnd_transport_dev+ spnd_food_dev+ spnd_housing_dev+ spnd_med_dev+ spnd_business_dev+ spnd_debt_dev + spnd_household_dev+ time_save_dev + spnd_clothes_dev + exp_material_mat_dev +  spnd_goods_dev+ spnd_indv_donation_dev+ spnd_edu_dev+ spnd_personal_dev+ exp_material_exp_dev+  spnd_org_donation_dev+ payment_amount_usd_stnd_dev + (1 | pid), data = df_spend_cent)
tab_model(mlm1,dv.labels = "Purchase-level happiness", pred.labels =  c("Intercept", "Utilities", "Transportation", "Essential food","Housing", "Medical", "Business items", "Debt", "Household items", "Time saving", "Clothes", "Material goods for entertainment", "Durable goods", "Gifts to an individual", "Education", "Personal care", "Experience", "Donation to organization", "Payment cost"), p.val = "kr", show.df = TRUE, show.stat = TRUE)
```

Plot
```{r}
# Figure 2
mlm1_tidy <- tidy(mlm1)
mlm1_tidy <- mlm1_tidy[-(19:21),]
mlm1_tidy <- mlm1_tidy[-(1),]

mlm1_tidy <-left_join(mlm1_tidy, titles_dev, by = c("term")) 
mlm1_tidy <- mlm1_tidy %>% select(-term) 
colnames(mlm1_tidy)[colnames(mlm1_tidy) == "title"] <- "term"


p1 <- mlm1_tidy %>% 
 arrange(desc(estimate)) %>% 
 dwplot(vline = geom_vline(
xintercept = 0,
colour = "grey60",
linetype = 2),
# dot_args = list(color = "black"),
# whisker_args = list(color = "black")
 whisker_args = list(aes(color = p.value < .05), size = 1),
 dot_args = list(aes(color = p.value < .05), size = 2)
) +
scale_color_manual(values = c("gray", "black")) +
theme_minimal() +
guides(color = guide_none()) +
labs(x = "Happiness")+ 
 theme(axis.title.x = element_text(size = 8))

p1

```

```{r}
ggsave("p1.png", width = 5, height = 3 )
```

# Comparison of windfall and using the money in happy ways

```{r}
summary(df_3monly_cash$payment_happy_comp_mean)
```
###Using money in ways that make a person happy
###3 months
Compute quintiles for average happiness with purchases
```{r}
quantiles <- c(0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8)
cut_off_points <- quantile(df_3monly_cash$payment_happy_comp_mean, quantiles)
print(cut_off_points)
```

Creating subset data of highest and lowest quintile
```{r}
df_3monly_cash_q1 <- df_3monly_cash %>% subset(payment_happy_comp_mean < 3.4)
df_3monly_cash_q5 <- df_3monly_cash %>% subset(payment_happy_comp_mean > 4.468750)
```

Computing the change in subjective well-being in the highest and lowest quintiles
```{r}
average_difference <- mean(df_3monly_cash_q1$swb - df_3monly_cash_q1$swb_bl, na.rm = TRUE)

print(average_difference)
```

```{r}
average_difference <- mean(df_3monly_cash_q5$swb - df_3monly_cash_q5$swb_bl, na.rm = TRUE)

print(average_difference)
```

```{r}
0.7832931 - 0.3117665
```

# Total amount spent per category and test statistics
Table S5
```{r}
# Compute the average (mean) of each specified column across all rows
averages_table <- df_spending_summary %>%
  select(spnd_clothes_total, spnd_debt_total, spnd_edu_total, spnd_food_total, spnd_goods_total, 
         spnd_household_total, spnd_housing_total, spnd_indv_donation_total, spnd_med_total, 
         spnd_org_donation_total, spnd_personal_total, spnd_transport_total, spnd_utility_total, 
         exp_material_exp_total, exp_material_mat_total, spnd_business_total, time_save_total) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), mean, na.rm = TRUE))

# View the resulting table with the averages
averages_table


```

## Country-level income
```{r}
# Compute the averages for each group in gdp_lo_hi
averages_by_gdp <- df_spending_summary %>%
  group_by(gdp_lo_hi) %>%
  summarise(across(c(spnd_clothes_total, spnd_debt_total, spnd_edu_total, spnd_food_total, spnd_goods_total, 
                     spnd_household_total, spnd_housing_total, spnd_indv_donation_total, spnd_med_total, 
                     spnd_org_donation_total, spnd_personal_total, spnd_transport_total, spnd_utility_total, 
                     exp_material_exp_total, exp_material_mat_total, spnd_business_total, time_save_total), 
                   mean, na.rm = TRUE))

# View the resulting table with the averages for each 'gdp_lo_hi' group
averages_by_gdp

# Function to compute both t-statistic and p-value for each variable
compute_t_stat_p_value <- function(var_name) {
  t_result <- t.test(df_spending_summary[[var_name]] ~ df_spending_summary$gdp_lo_hi, na.rm = TRUE)
  return(c(t_statistic = t_result$statistic, p_value = t_result$p.value))
}

# Compute t-statistics and p-values for each variable
t_stats_p_values <- sapply(variables, compute_t_stat_p_value)

# Convert the t-stats and p-values into a data frame for easier manipulation
t_stats_p_values_df <- as.data.frame(t(t_stats_p_values))
t_stats_p_values_df$variable <- rownames(t_stats_p_values_df)

# Combine means, t-statistics, and p-values into a single table
results_table <- averages_by_gdp %>%
  pivot_longer(-gdp_lo_hi, names_to = "variable", values_to = "mean_value") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = gdp_lo_hi, values_from = mean_value) %>%
  left_join(t_stats_p_values_df, by = "variable") %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(., 3)))  # Round all numeric values to 3 decimals

# View the results
results_table


```

```{r}
write_xlsx(results_table, "averages_and_t_statistics.xlsx")
```

## Public vs. private
```{r}

# Compute the average for each condition (private vs public)
averages_by_condition <- df_spending_summary %>%
  group_by(condition) %>%
  summarise(across(c(spnd_clothes_total, spnd_debt_total, spnd_edu_total, spnd_food_total, 
                     spnd_goods_total, spnd_household_total, spnd_housing_total, 
                     spnd_indv_donation_total, spnd_med_total, spnd_org_donation_total, 
                     spnd_personal_total, spnd_transport_total, spnd_utility_total, 
                     exp_material_exp_total, exp_material_mat_total, spnd_business_total, 
                     time_save_total), 
                   mean, na.rm = TRUE))

# Function to compute both t-statistic and p-value for each variable by condition
compute_t_stat_p_value_condition <- function(var_name) {
  t_result <- t.test(df_spending_summary[[var_name]] ~ df_spending_summary$condition, na.rm = TRUE)
  return(c(t_statistic = t_result$statistic, p_value = t_result$p.value))
}

# List of variables to compute t-tests for
variables <- c("spnd_clothes_total", "spnd_debt_total", "spnd_edu_total", "spnd_food_total", 
               "spnd_goods_total", "spnd_household_total", "spnd_housing_total", 
               "spnd_indv_donation_total", "spnd_med_total", "spnd_org_donation_total", 
               "spnd_personal_total", "spnd_transport_total", "spnd_utility_total", 
               "exp_material_exp_total", "exp_material_mat_total", "spnd_business_total", 
               "time_save_total")

# Compute t-statistics and p-values for each variable by condition
t_stats_p_values_condition <- sapply(variables, compute_t_stat_p_value_condition)

# Convert the t-stats and p-values into a data frame for easier manipulation
t_stats_p_values_df_condition <- as.data.frame(t(t_stats_p_values_condition))
t_stats_p_values_df_condition$variable <- rownames(t_stats_p_values_df_condition)

# Combine means, t-statistics, and p-values into a single table
results_table_condition <- averages_by_condition %>%
  pivot_longer(-condition, names_to = "variable", values_to = "mean_value") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = mean_value) %>%
  left_join(t_stats_p_values_df_condition, by = "variable") %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(., 3)))  # Round all numeric values to 3 decimals

# View the results
results_table_condition

```

```{r}
write_xlsx(results_table_condition, "averages_and_t_statistics_cond.xlsx")
```

#Plot with individual data points

```{r}
# List of variable names in the desired order to have donations at the top
columns <- c(
  'spnd_utility', 'spnd_transport', 'spnd_food',
  'spnd_housing', 'spnd_med', 'spnd_business', 'spnd_debt',
  'spnd_household', 'time_save', 'spnd_clothes', 'exp_material_mat', 
  'spnd_goods', 'spnd_indv_donation', 'spnd_edu', 'spnd_personal', 'exp_material_exp', 'spnd_org_donation'
)

# Use match to get the labels in the new order of `columns`
labels <- titles_spnd$title[match(columns, titles_spnd$term)]

# Filter and melt the data for categories with value 1
df_melted <- df_spend_cent %>%
  select(all_of(columns), payment_happy_comp) %>%
  melt(id.vars = 'payment_happy_comp', variable.name = 'Category', value.name = 'Value') %>%
  filter(Value == 1)

# Convert Category to a factor with levels and labels from the new order
df_melted$Category <- factor(df_melted$Category, levels = columns, labels = labels)

# Create a plot with individual, smaller data points, spread out more vertically
my_plot <- ggplot(df_melted, aes(x = payment_happy_comp, y = Category)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1, height = 0.4, alpha = 0.6, size = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "Plot of Happiness by Spending Category with Individual Data Points", x = "Happiness", y = "") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5))

my_plot
```

```{r}
# Save the plot with 300 DPI
ggsave("individual_points_plot.png", plot = my_plot, dpi = 300, height = 6, width = 8, units = "in")
```
